chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from Sulaymān al-Jaʿfarī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
All sins are grave, and the gravest of them is that upon which flesh and blood have grown, because it is either shown mercy or punished, and none enters Paradise except one who is pure.

key_terms.الدَّمُ: blood, indicating what becomes integrated into the body
key_terms.اللَّحْمُ: flesh, referring to the body nourished by what one consumes
key_terms.طَيِّبٌ: pure, wholesome, and purified from defilement

ai.seo_question: Which sins are described as the most severe in this hadith from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that all sins are serious, but the most severe are those connected to what nourishes the body, meaning what becomes part of one's flesh and blood. It also emphasizes accountability in the Hereafter and that entry into Paradise belongs only to the purified and wholesome.
